newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street slightly higher in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street slightly higher in choppy trade.

text.p: Wall Street shares were slightly higher in early-afternoon trade Wednesday following a choppy morning that saw blue chips slip on profit-taking, recover amid bargain-hunting and window-dressing, then slide again.
The Dow industrials seesawed for much of the morning, at one point rising sharply and prompting the New York Stock Exchange to impose curbs on index-arbitrage trades.
The curbs were lifted at 1222 EDT/1622 GMT as the Dow began a new retreat.
At 1307 EDT/1707 GMT the index was up 13 points at 7771, well below its session high of 7812 but well above its session low of 7710.

"The market is somewhat directionless here and it should be," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "It is reflecting both the positive and the negative news on the economic front today..."
Durable goods orders for May declined 0.6 percent, versus an expected rise, but non-defense capital goods orders rose.
Bonds and stocks took that data in stride, but bonds were thrown off course by a jump in U.S. existing home sales.

The National Association of Realtors reported that sales of existing homes rose 4.4 percent in May to an annual rate of 4.24 million, well above Wall Street economists' forecasts for a 4.07 million rate.
"Keep your eye on the bond market," said Frank Calta, managing director of institutional trading at Dain Bosworth.
While the stock market was reacting to nervous moves in the bond market, it was also boosted by money managers buying stocks and adjusting portfolios ahead of the quarter's close, analysts said.

"There are two forces at work in this market," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "The positive force is that portfolio managers are trying to buy their favorite stocks at the quarter end; But on the negative side, the bond market looks tired."
As soon as the stock market declined, investors rushed back in, analysts said.
"This market is driven by optimism," said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer of Amas Securities.
First Albany's Johnson said optimism was partly created by the good outlook for corporate earnings.
Data that indicated economic strength, and consequently spooked inflation-wary bonds, reinforced the idea that "earnings estimates are on solid footing," he said.
Greg Nie, a technical analyst at EVEREN Securities Inc, said the stock market's biggest gains had been accompanied by heavy volume, a bullish sign.
Among the day's highlights, Liposome Co sank after the company said its lead product in development failed to demonstrate efficacy in Phase III clinical trials.
3Com Corp was down 1-1/4 at 48-1/2 in brisk trade. The company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.48 per share, compared to $0.46 per fully diluted share before a pretax charge of $0.30.
3Com said it expects results for the first quarter ending in August to show slower revenue growth because of slowing sales in Europe and work necessary to merge recently-acquired U.S. Robotics Corp.
Boeing Co was up 13/16 at 55-13/16. The Wall Street Journal said Boeing might change several sole-supplier pacts with U.S. airlines to pacify European regulators.
((--Wall Street Desk 212-859-1730))
